card.content:
🤫 **Ember is hushed.** Hush is the quietest of three modes — it stops *sound*, not listening. Tap the screen and Ember still hears you, still thinks, and still answers; the reply arrives **on screen**, headed `UNSPOKEN`, with the sub-line *the reply is on screen*. Chimes are silent too.

It does **not** mute the microphone and does **not** gate the talk gesture — that was the old meaning of this switch and it changed on 2026-07-30. Pushed announcements still arrive as text and leave an unread pip until you touch the screen.

Set **Mode** to `Normal` to give Ember its voice back, or `No talking` to keep chimes without speech.

⚠ **Speaker Volume is not reporting.** The DAC-volume control arrives with the firmware that adds `number: spk_volume` — flash the device config and this tile self-heals. Until then the es8311 boots at `set_volume(0.75)` = 0 dB, which is the *too loud* default.
*The box is empty, so **Speak it** will do nothing* — `script.ember_say` conditions on there being text and aborts quietly rather than announcing silence. Type something first.

cards.content:
**Speak it** runs `script.ember_say`, which reads the field above and hands it to `script.ember_announce` — never `assist_satellite.announce` directly, because the script pins `preannounce: false` and without it HA prepends its own generic blip so you hear two heralds back to back.

The field-plus-button pairing exists because Lovelace `perform_action` data is **not** templated: a button cannot carry a text field's contents, only call something that reads it. 255 characters, `input_text`'s hard cap.

card.content: ⚠ **Mic Gain is not reporting.** The ADC-PGA control arrives with the firmware that adds `number: mic_gain_num` — flash the device config and this tile self-heals. Until then the es8311 runs the compile-time `mic_gain: 36db` from its `audio_dac` block, which is the same value, just not adjustable.

⚠ **The control below is showing a value the codec does not hold.** `Mic Gain` reads **{{ states('number.ember_satellite_mic_gain') | float(0) | round(0) | int }} dB**, while the es8311's REG16 reads **{{ states('sensor.ember_satellite_mic_gain_codec') | float(0) | round(0) | int }} dB**.

Believe the codec figure — it is read back off the chip, not reported by the entity. Either something wrote REG16 without going through the number, or a restore did not reach it. The firmware re-checks every 60 s, so this clears itself once they agree.

*Mic parked.* `sound_level` publishes NAN whenever the microphone isn't running — during TTS, and any time Ember isn't listening — so the gauges hide rather than render a non-numeric error. They return the moment a level arrives.

cards.heading: Persona · a live nudge to the prompt

cards.content:
Typed here, appended to the **very end** of Ember's prompt and live on the next turn. Try *“Be even terser today, one sentence only.”*

255 characters — that's `input_text`'s hard cap, not a choice. Full persona edits live at **Settings → Devices & Services → Ember (familiar local) → the conversation subentry → Reconfigure**.

The trailing placement is load-bearing, not arbitrary: the prompt prefix has to stay byte-stable for llama.cpp to reuse its KV cache (~1.7 s warm instead of ~7.6 s), and mid-prompt the model ignored this field outright. Don't move it earlier.

cards.heading: Ear · sound level, last hour · all hearths

cards.content: Calibrated dBFS from ESPHome's `sound_level` component (`passive: true` — it never starts or stops the mic, so it cannot contend with `voice_assistant` over the shared I²S hub). The device's own waveform is scaled `-72 dB → -30 dB`; these gauges use the same floor and ceiling. Reads *unknown* while TTS is playing — `sound_level` publishes NAN whenever the mic isn't running.

**Only the mobile board has a cell.** `sensor.ember_satellite_battery_voltage` and `sensor.ember_dad_battery_voltage` exist — the GPIO9 ADC is unconditional in the shared firmware — but on a mains board they read an *absent divider*. They sit around **4.1 V**, which looks exactly like a healthy lithium cell and is not one.

⚠ *They are deliberately not charted here, and were removed from this view on 2026-08-09.* The firmware already refuses to expose SOC on a cell-less board for this reason (see `esphome/ember-mobile.yaml`); this view now agrees with it. **Do not “restore” them.**

cards.heading: Speech liveness · frames pushed to the DAC · all hearths

cards.content:
During TTS this climbs at **16000/s**, and that is now a measured baseline rather than a target: a 27.2 s announcement produced **26 consecutive one-second windows at exactly +16000 frames, 99.84 % cumulative, zero injected silence.** Long utterances used to land between 45.8 % and 93.9 %, so a shortfall here is a real regression, not normal variance.

A flat line while Ember is *responding* means `audio_output_callback_` never reaches the counter — usually a resampler or mixer sitting between `voice_assistant` and `spk`. Exact only to ~16.7 M frames (float mantissa); diagnostic only, the display maths uses the `uint32_t` directly.

cards.heading: Mind · the local Qwen lane on familiar

cards.content: `binary_sensor.ember_backend` polls llama.cpp's `/health` every 60 s and goes *unavailable* when the host doesn't answer at all; `ember_reachable` collapses that into on/off plus a readable `detail`, so no card has to special-case `unavailable`. Over 24 h this graph is effectively **familiar's sleep log** — the host S3-suspends itself after ~15 min idle. Polling does not keep it awake (autosuspend watches whether the inference lane is loaded, not network traffic), so a gap here is a true signal rather than an artefact of measuring.

cards.name: Screen not responding? Rouse the touch sensor
Mode · how much noise Ember may make
BOOT button (the only one on the PCB)

cards.content:
**Rouse** re-pulses the FT6336G's reset line and re-runs its setup — the recovery for a touchscreen that has stopped answering. It is deliberately reachable from *here* rather than only on the device, because recovering the touchscreen must not require the touchscreen. Takes ~310 ms and will log a *took a long time* warning; that's expected for a manual recovery action.

**BOOT** is the entire hardware input budget of this board (K1/K2 are RESET and BOOT; RESET is wired to CHIP_PU and can't be read). Short-press summons Ember or steps the volume overlay; it also drives the power menu, so it can reach Rouse without touch.

data.message: The hearth is lit, and my mind is my own.
This is the portable hearth, and I am lit.

cards.content: `ember_announce_if_awake` speaks only when the local lane is reachable, and otherwise logs the skip rather than announcing into a void. Pressing this while `Reachability` above reads *serving* should speak; with familiar asleep it should stay silent and leave a warning in the log.

The media_player is why HA can push speech at all: `FEATURE_ANNOUNCE` is gated strictly on `voice_assistant` owning one, which is what moved the satellite's `supported_features` **0 → 3**. Announcement pipeline only — no media pipeline, so no mixer is needed.

⚠ *This slider is not the loudness control.* It sets the announcement **pipeline** level, an earlier stage; the es8311 DAC volume on the Hearth view (`Hearth Voice · Output Level`) is the one that governs how loud Ember actually is, and it applies to conversational replies too. Reach for that one first.

**A faint pop on the mic/speaker hand-off is expected and bounded** — not a fault, and not worth re-investigating. ESPHome tears down and recreates the I²S clock on every hand-off, while vendor firmware (Korvo, xiaozhi) holds duplex channels open and never stops it. Every ES8311 anti-pop mechanism is clocked by LRCK, so none of them can survive the restart of their own clock. Removing it means leaving stock ESPHome behind.
